title: Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
summary: Anomaly detection methods struggle with data exhibiting varying local densities, where distance-based methods miss local anomalies and density-based methods require careful parameter selection and incur quadratic time complexity. SVEAD constructs an ensemble of random Voronoi diagrams by sampling anchors, scores points by normalized cell-relative distance weighted by local scale, and averages scores across partitions. Across 45 ADBench datasets it achieves the highest average AUC-ROC (0.8538) and AUC-PR (0.5000) among 12 baselines, including 0.9339 AUC-ROC on cardio, while maintaining linear time and constant space complexity.

requirements.stmt: Sample m anchors uniformly from the dataset without replacement for each partition.
requirements.quote: we randomly sample m points from the dataset X without replacement to form an anchor set

requirements.stmt: Assign each point to its nearest anchor using Euclidean distance, without building explicit Voronoi cells.
requirements.quote: Each point x ∈X is assigned to its nearest anchor, creating a partition

requirements.stmt: Compute the within-cell score as the normalized relative distance times the cell's mean anchor distance.
requirements.quote: where the first term δ/δmax normalizes the distance by the maximum cell radius, and the second term δmean represents the mean distance within the cell.

requirements.stmt: For each cell, compute the maximum and mean distances from its anchor before scoring.
requirements.quote: computing cell statistics including maximum and mean distances.

requirements.stmt: Skip a point in a partition when its cell contains only the anchor, relying on the remaining partitions.
requirements.quote: In the rare case where a cell contains only the anchor (|Ci| = 1), we skip scoring for this point in this partition

requirements.stmt: Aggregate per-partition scores by arithmetic mean over the t partitions.
requirements.quote: The final anomaly score is computed as the arithmetic mean:

requirements.stmt: Tune the number of sampled anchors m by grid search and fix ensemble size t at 100.
requirements.quote: the number of sample points is searched over {21, 22, . . . , 28}, with ensemble size fixed at 100.

requirements.stmt: Repeat each dataset-method experiment 5 times and report the average.
requirements.quote: For each dataset and method, we repeat experiments 5 times and report the average performance.

requirements.stmt: Use AUC-ROC and AUC-PR as the evaluation metrics.
requirements.quote: We adopt Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) and Area Under the Precision-Recall curve (AUC-PR) in the experiment.

requirements.stmt: Use labels only after anomaly scores are produced, preserving the unsupervised setting.
requirements.quote: the labels are used to compute the AUC-ROC and AUC-PR for each dataset only after the models have made predictions.

requirements.stmt: Implement implicit Voronoi diagrams via nearest-anchor queries rather than explicit cell-boundary construction.
requirements.quote: we do not compute cell boundaries or vertices; we only determine point-to-cell membership through nearest-anchor queries.

requirements.stmt: Maintain linear time complexity in the number of points, anchors, dimensions, and ensemble size.
requirements.quote: The total time complexity is O(nmdt) + O(nmdt) = O(nmdt)
